decisions: A spoken command is the authorization (owner decision, 14 October, replacing 7 October's "voice leaves a card" after review): realtime voice runs an action that needs approval when asked, audited as approved by voice, as before Q-08 and as main's #1006 has it. A tainted session's approvals, cards that must be clicked and the blocked categories are still refused; with no primary agent nothing runs.
Main's current voice room-action safeguards are retained: Authority grants and revokes require clicks; workflow starts and agent actions keep their own gates.

Pause holds, Kill stops (owner decision). Pause: nothing new starts or continues; queued and waiting work waits; a scheduled time is skipped and shown; a webhook is told to retry later; approving a card waits for Resume; a run already executing parks at its next step and Resume releases it. Kill: also stops every unfinished run, denies pending work approvals while preserving Stop agent cards and stops tools in flight at their next dispatch checkpoint; Reset starts nothing again.
Owner approved main's stricter chat safeguards on 14 October: both approve and deny require a sender on the current channel allow-list, an exact 8-character ID, and one matching card.

Defaults: an unanswered chat or background card expires after 24 hours (workflow approvals keep their own lifecycle); community pieces and CODE steps stay opt-in, without per-run approval, but obey Pause and Kill and are audited.
behavior: An approval request records whom it was asked for (role, level, profile). When the approved call runs, the executor judges it again as that agent, the way its gate did, with the approval standing in for the approval it asked for: a deny override, a context rule or a revoked permission added since the card was raised stops it. A request from before records no one and is asked for again.

A card that must be reviewed on screen (browser and desktop actions) is approved on the dashboard only: a chat reply, a toast or a spoken yes is refused, saying why, and the card stays pending; its desktop notification offers Review in Jarvis instead of Approve; and the executor refuses an approval from anywhere else.
Two surfaces deciding one request dispatch it once (compare-and-set decision, one execution claim), now tested through the shared decision path.

Approving while Jarvis is paused or stopped is refused, saying so, and the card stays pending for Resume: a refused notification shows the card again with the reason, and the dashboard shows the server's reason. Denying works. Running an approval a restart left unresolved waits the same way.

Realtime voice: a spoken command is the authorization (owner decision, 14 October), so a call that needs approval runs, audited as approval_required and executed; a tainted session's approval, a click-only card and the blocked categories are refused; with no primary agent the gate fails closed.

A request_approval the person did not approve (denied, expired or unanswered) governs its category for the rest of the turn, so a later tool call in it needs its own approval. A task cancelled while its card waits withdraws the card, and the dashboard drops it. A spoken yes or no decides nothing while more than one card waits.

Pause and Kill below every UI control: tool dispatch refuses at the agent gates (existing) and, on Kill, at every dispatch checkpoint inside a running tool; the workflow worker claims nothing; a job claimed as the pause began goes back untouched; Kill stops every unfinished run and denies pending work approvals while preserving Stop agent cards; triggers start nothing (a scheduled time is recorded as skipped, keyed so it is not run late; a webhook gets 503 with Retry-After; an event source is not polled, so its items wait, and items a poll had already taken are queued for Resume); timers, approvals and resume URLs wake nothing (a resume URL answers 503 while paused, 409 under Kill); starting a run by hand (dashboard, chat, work item) is refused, saying why; a governed workflow step, a community piece or a CODE step reached while paused parks on a HOLD waitpoint that Resume releases (a resume URL never can, and none is listed for it), and then runs as it was about to: from the start if it had not run, or resuming its own pause with its payload, so a Delay still waits its full time; a recorded piece or delegation authorization is not handed out again while paused or stopped.

The emergency controller is the one source of truth: the engine's copy of the state follows every change (it was the boot snapshot, which kept workflows blocked after Resume), a learning accept no longer writes the state back (which could turn a Kill to normal across a restart), and every change is audited.

A governed piece's approval binds a digest of the whole resolved input, connection excluded, alongside the card's projection: a longer body or more recipients than the card could show need a new approval. An effect recorded before this build, without the digest, is matched without it once and bound to it from then on.

Receipts stay distinct: a tool that could not say whether it took effect leaves the request unresolved (unknown, never run again, closed by a person); nothing started is blocked, not failed. Chat replies, the dashboard notification, the tray and the Task complete toast say what the receipt says. Every decision a person makes is audited with its surface (click, chat, notification, voice) and every receipt, refusals included, with its outcome. A community piece or CODE step leaves an admission row recording the dispatch; Jarvis's own pieces (audited at the boundary) and built-in steps leave none. Unanswered cards expire after 24 hours and leave the dashboard.

A config change is validated before it is applied, and a level that is not a number counts for nothing (it used to pass every level check). A learning suggestion can be accepted only if the learner made it.
Work-item runs check the workflow's CODE-step grant, as every other start does.

manual_checks: Not run against a live daemon: no real provider, browser, desktop or voice session is needed for these fixtures (delivery contract). The quick path below names the manual checks for a dev daemon.

quick_verify.manual: On a dev daemon: press Pause while a workflow runs a step just before a one-minute Delay, then Resume (the delay starts after Resume and waits its full minute); press Kill with a run queued and a card pending (the run is stopped and the card denied, each saying why); in a voice session ask for something that needs approval (it runs, and the audit trail shows it approved by voice); approve a browser-action card from Telegram (refused: approve it on the dashboard); press Approve on a desktop notification while paused (it comes back saying Jarvis is paused).
quick_verify.screenshot: not taken: the visible changes are text (a refusal reason on a card, a stat label, a waitpoint line)

migration: Additive: column approval_requests.principal, waitpoint type HOLD and the jarvisParked key in a parked step's output. A pending request created before this build has no principal; if approved, it is refused when it runs and asked for again. A governed piece effect recorded before this build is matched without the whole-input digest once, then bound to it.
rollback: Revert the Q-08 commits. The column, the waitpoint type and the output key are additive and ignored by older builds. Resume Jarvis before rolling back: a HOLD waitpoint left by a run parked while paused is not released by an older build.
limitations: Voice can still press dashboard buttons that change permissions or start work (owner decision).
Community pieces run with Jarvis's own permissions and can read any saved connection: the Library's opt-in trust model, unchanged.
A delegated agent's allowed calls are checked but not listed as run effects (Q-10).
Approval cards show what will happen, not the raw arguments (dashboard work).

Kill stops a tool at its next dispatch checkpoint: one command already running on a machine finishes. A sub-agent started by a tool stops at its next turn. A tool stopped this way is recorded as "may have happened", even at its first checkpoint, since a checkpoint cannot tell whether an earlier dispatch took place; a card caught there is closed by a person.
Under Kill a webhook sender is still told to retry, so a retry after Reset starts a run; scheduled times during Kill stay skipped.
On macOS a notification for a click-only card still shows Approve (macOS sets the buttons by kind); pressing it brings the card back saying to approve it on the dashboard.
An intent grant (request_approval) is recorded as executed.
Opportunity activation has no route of its own; accepted work items start through the run route.
The 24-hour expiry, the Kill and Resume wiring and the notification handling in daemon/index.ts are thin calls into tested functions; the daemon process itself is not started by the tests.
found: An approved request ran under the permissions in force when it was raised: tightening permissions afterwards did not stop it, inline, deferred or after a restart.
Realtime voice ran ungated and unaudited when no primary agent was active.
A click-only review card could be approved from Telegram, Discord or a toast; only voice refused it.

Kill only changed a flag: nothing stopped runs, denied pending approvals or interrupted tools, and the engine's copy of the state was the boot snapshot (workflows stayed blocked after Resume until a restart, and a learning accept could write a Kill back to normal).

Under Pause the workflow worker kept claiming jobs, triggers kept starting runs, timers, approvals and resume URLs kept waking runs, and an approved step reached while paused was refused for good instead of held.
Community pieces and CODE steps never asked the daemon anything, so no Pause or Kill applied to them, and they left no audit row.
A piece approval bound a projection cut twice (512 characters, 25 items, 40 keys, depth 5), so a longer body or more recipients ran under an approval for fewer.
A recorded piece or delegation authorization was handed out again before any check, including during an emergency.
A tool that could not say whether it took effect was recorded as failed; blocked runs, intent grants and authorizations read as executed in replies, toasts and the tray.

A denied request_approval did not stop the same action through a tool the level allowed; a cancelled task's card stayed approvable; cards never expired; a spoken yes approved the newest card across all agents.
POST /api/authority/config accepted a non-number level, which passed every level check; learning accept added an always-allow override for any action.
Work-item runs skipped the CODE-step grant check.
integration: Rebased onto Q-06 134f23ddaf510e697297214fa028fe18f6653b42, which includes main 5024ea7455a5613be0514475be32c0dee6de0edd. Existing stacked PR targets are preserved.

Owner approved combining execution-time Authority rechecks with main's approval guards, current channel allow-list, exact short-ID matching, toast readability protections, voice card binding and realtime per-category approval scope.

Lifecycle Spawn and Stop cards now record the requesting agent's role, authority level and effective profile. The executor rechecks current rules; older cards without that identity require a fresh request.

Owner approved Kill stopping queued, running and waiting workflows, denying other pending work cards, and preserving Stop agent cards during Pause and Kill. Reset revives no stopped run or denied work.

Main's real lifecycle tests now wire the Authority engine into DeferredExecutor, and tests exercise Stop agent through the shared decision handler with the active emergency controller. The initial regression run demonstrated the missing-principal and held-stop failures before the fixes.

Click-only notifications use main's approval_review kind and preserve the full action sentence and readability guards. Main channel and notification handlers retain Q-08's execution outcome reporting and decision audit.

Main's newer bundle-integrity check is preserved by passing expectedDigest in the real engine test. Main's delegated-agent Kill cancellation and full-input approval digest are retained in the adapted regressions.

The pinned main's registry has no observeToolExecution wrapper; the rebase retains its existing dispatch and cancellation behavior under Q-08's kill fence. Main's outsideExecutionScope and delegated-call approval scope are retained.
next: Bind delegated-agent effects to their approval receipts (Q-10), show raw arguments on approval cards, and isolate community pieces from saved connections. The Kill and approval integration decisions for this rebase are approved.
